recall.minute: Off-policy methods learn about a target policy π from episodes of a behaviour policy b (a doctor's records vs a proposed protocol), requiring coverage: π(a|s) > 0 ⇒ b(a|s) > 0. Returns are reweighted by the importance-sampling ratio ρ = Π π/b; the transition probabilities cancel, so no model is needed, and E_b[ρG] = v_π. With π = (0.8, 0.7, 0.8) and b = (0.5, 0.4, 0.5), ρ = 4.48. Ordinary IS divides Σ ρG by the number of visits (unbiased, possibly infinite variance); weighted IS divides by Σ ρ (biased but consistent and stable). Returns (4.24, 2.61, 2.33) with weights (6.667, 0.125, 1.5) give OIS 10.70 (outside the observed range) and WIS 3.87. In the one-state loop example (target always left, behaviour 50/50) the second moment Σ 0.2·1.8ᵏ⁻¹ diverges. Effective sample size (ΣW)²/ΣW² (1.47 here) flags dominant weights. Incremental WIS: C ← C + W, V ← V + (W/C)(G − V) (5 → 4 → 4). Off-policy MC control updates Q backwards with weighted IS, makes π greedy, and breaks at the first non-greedy action, so only episode tails teach the target.
